focus.jbig: Democratic sweep resolved cleanly · relief rally · VIX down ~12% · AI-rotation tape · 7 setups boarded
focus.jtag: Democrats took both chambers and Trump said he'd accept the result, flipping a −1.4% futures scare into a buy-the-dip bounce; the VIX fell ~12% toward 18 as the one-day election premium bled out. The scanner boarded ANET, CRCL & DDOG (Type A) plus LNG, MO, MA and SPOT (Type C breakouts)
focus.jnote: The overnight unknown resolved about as cleanly as it could. US equity index futures rallied, reversing earlier losses, after the Democrats swept to power in Congress and President Trump said he would accept the results, easing uncertainty and prompting investors to buy the recent dip. S&P 500 contracts traded 0.8% higher, having earlier fallen as much as 1.4%, while Nasdaq 100 futures erased a drop that had reached 2.4%. The S&P 500 climbed 27.52 points, or 0.36%, to 7,568.92 on Tuesday. Vol is deflating fast: the VIX is down 12% at 18.31 and the front of the volatility curve has come in, with the inversion of the last two weeks gone. But under the hood it's a rotation, not an all-clear: banks, health insurers, equal weight, Europe's lenders, China and the miners are up, while the data-centre complex, defence and the Musk names are down. An index up 1% with its leaders down is a tape that is rotating, and rotations last longer than reflex rallies. Calmer than yesterday, but still a half-size tape.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the held breakouts in non-AI groups are the cleanest fit for a rotation tape. MO (Altria), MA (Mastercard) and LNG (Cheniere) are all low-to-mid-beta held breakouts outside the data-center complex that is being sold today. ANET is the standout Type A fundamentally — revenue rose 58.5% to $3.66 billion, beating the $3.33 billion estimate, with adjusted EPS of $1.20 beating by $0.12 — but it's an AI-infrastructure name squarely in the rotation's crosshairs. On a WARM, half-size day every one is watch-only, A-grade and confirmed-at-9:35 only.
focus.notup: Two Type A names are tagged bearish — but mind the live tape. The scanner boarded CRCL and DDOG as bearish gap-downs, yet this morning Circle reported adjusted EPS of $0.84, and shares were up 3.26% in pre-market trading following the announcement — a bullish reaction that contradicts the bearish tag, so a bear call there is fighting the move. DDOG is the opposite: Datadog beat expectations with revenue up 35.2% to $1.20 billion but the stock dropped 16.1% on soft large-contract wins, confirming the bearish gap — but selling bear calls into a VIX-collapsing relief bounce invites a squeeze. Treat both as watch-only.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? The clean, Trump-accepted sweep removed the worst overnight tail and the VIX fell ~12%, which argues against RED. But P(≥1% gap) at ~36% is still a hair above the 35% trigger — that alone locks out GREEN — and composite ~52 sits in WARM, with an active AI-capex rotation and ADP private payrolls plus ISM Services today keeping the tape two-sided. Every Type A gap here printed on light relative volume and every Type C is a 2–3-session-old breakout. Half size, A-grade only, 7-DTE that clears the data, and keep every spread clear of its name's next print.

risks: AI-capex rotation — the data-centre complex, defence and the Musk names are down while banks, health and miners are up; an index up 1% with its leaders down is a rotating tape, and rotations last longer than reflex rallies. This is the number-one thing to watch under the hood.

ADP private payrolls & ISM Services today — the data cluster can whip rates and risk intraday; a hot services print would re-arm higher-for-longer fear just as the election premium bleeds out. A scheduled event any 7-DTE spread must clear.
DDOG's 17% air-pocket — Datadog beat but fell 16.1% with no S/R layers within 18% of price; on a VIX-falling relief day that kind of oversold gap is prime squeeze material against any bear call.

Post-election policy overhang — index futures fell overnight on concern that a Democratic Congress brings tighter scrutiny of technology and AI spending. The reflex bounce can fade if that scrutiny narrative reasserts on the AI names.
Gap math still above trigger — P(≥1% gap) ~36% sits a hair above the 35% line and composite ~52 is in WARM; even with the election resolved, that keeps GREEN locked out and the day a half-size tape.
